stories.headline: The perfect storm behind the Nasdaq's rout — plus, some of the bright spots in the market
stories.summary: Tech stocks are selling off sharply as investors rotate out of AI-exposed names into defensive sectors. Despite the weakness, select data center plays and infrastructure beneficiaries are showing resilience.
stories.why_matters: Sector rotation signals shifting risk appetite and potential implications for growth equity valuations and duration positioning.

stories.headline: Jobless claims near the lowest since the 1960s as low-fire trend continues
stories.summary: US labor market remains exceptionally tight with jobless claims hovering near historic lows, defying recession concerns. The persistent strength in employment supports consumer spending but complicates Fed pivot expectations.
stories.why_matters: Ultra-low jobless claims sustain wage pressure and inflation dynamics, keeping the 10Y yield elevated despite today's 3bp decline.

stories.headline: Gulf markets fall as fresh Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia raise regional risk
stories.summary: Renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East from Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure elevate oil supply risk premiums. Citi warns upside risks remain skewed higher for crude despite current Gulf export recovery.
stories.why_matters: Oil supply shocks and stagflationary tail risks drive commodity volatility that can sustain real rates and complicate monetary policy outlook.

concept.title: Rotation Amid Rate Persistence
concept.one_liner: Equities sell off while the long end holds firm as labor strength keeps terminal rates elevated despite AI sector weakness.
concept.explanation: The S&P 500's 1.43% decline paired with a steeper 2Y (+2bps) versus 10Y (-3bps) curve reflects investor rotation out of growth names into defensives. Jobless claims at 1960s lows signal continued wage pressure, anchoring long rates despite equity weakness and a VIX decline. This disconnect—risk-off equities but sticky rates—is characteristic of stagflation concerns rather than pure recession fears.
concept.market_link: 10Y sticky at 5.12% despite equity selloff suggests Fed hold bias persists; rate-sensitive sectors underperform while defensives outperform in a 'lower for longer' growth scenario.

narrative: Equities declined 1.43% as the Nasdaq's AI rout accelerated sector rotation into defensives, yet the 10Y Treasury held firm at 5.12% (-3bps only) because ultra-tight labor conditions—jobless claims near 1960s lows—continue to anchor inflation expectations and rate terminal assumptions. The S&P's weakness without a sharp yield collapse underscores market anxiety about stagflationary persistence rather than recession imminent.
